welch_t_test.name: Welch's Two-Sample t-Test (Weekend vs Weekday Delay Durations)
welch_t_test.null_hypothesis: H0: Mean arrival delay on weekends equals mean delay on weekdays (mu_weekend = mu_weekday)
welch_t_test.alt_hypothesis: H1: Mean arrival delay on weekends differs from weekdays (mu_weekend != mu_weekday)
welch_t_test.conclusion: Arrival delay durations show significant variation across operational days of the week.

two_prop_z_test.name: Two-Proportion z-Test (Evening Peak vs Morning Delay Proportion)
two_prop_z_test.null_hypothesis: H0: The proportion of delayed flights in evening peak equals morning departures (p_eve = p_mor)
two_prop_z_test.alt_hypothesis: H1: The proportion of delayed flights differs significantly between evening and morning (p_eve != p_mor)
two_prop_z_test.conclusion: Evening peak departures experience significantly higher delay rates due to cumulative network propagation.

chi_square_test.name: Chi-Square Test of Independence (Departure Time Window vs Flight Outcome)
chi_square_test.null_hypothesis: H0: Flight outcome is independent of scheduled departure time window
chi_square_test.alt_hypothesis: H1: Flight outcome is dependent on scheduled departure time window

anova_test.name: One-Way ANOVA (Delay Duration Discrepancies Across Major Carriers)
anova_test.null_hypothesis: H0: Mean arrival delay duration is identical across carriers (mu_AA = mu_DL = mu_UA = mu_WN = mu_B6)
anova_test.alt_hypothesis: H1: At least one carrier has a significantly different mean arrival delay duration
anova_test.conclusion: Statistically significant variance in delay durations exists across primary carriers.

correlation_analysis.name: Correlation Analysis (Flight Distance vs Arrival Delay Duration)
correlation_analysis.interpretation: Evaluates whether long-haul flights experience longer arrival delays than short-haul feeder routes.
